questions.prompt: What does an Elastic Load Balancer's health check accomplish?

options.text: It routes traffic only to healthy targets, taking failed servers out of rotation
It doubles the size of each server

questions.explanation: Health checks let the load balancer send requests only to healthy targets, so a failed server is automatically bypassed and users stay served.

questions.prompt: Which load balancer works at Layer 7 and can route by URL path or host?
questions.explanation: The Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and supports content-based routing by path or host. The NLB is a Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) balancer.

questions.prompt: What does an Auto Scaling group do when an instance fails its health check?

options.text: Nothing — you must fix it manually
It automatically replaces the unhealthy instance to maintain the desired capacity

questions.explanation: An ASG self-heals: it terminates unhealthy instances and launches replacements to keep the desired count across the chosen AZs.

questions.prompt: Why must servers be stateless to scale horizontally?

options.text: Any instance may serve any request and instances can be added or replaced, so local session state would be lost
It has no effect on scaling

questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling assumes any instance can handle any request. If session state lives on one instance, scaling out or replacing a failed instance loses it — so state belongs in a shared store.

questions.prompt: Adding or removing whole instances to handle load is called ____ scaling (as opposed to vertical).
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scale out/in) adds or removes instances; vertical scaling (scale up/down) moves to a bigger or smaller instance type.

questions.prompt: Match each scaling policy or term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Keep a metric like CPU at a set value
The instance count the ASG maintains
How each instance in the group is built

questions.explanation: Target tracking holds a metric at a target, scheduled scaling changes capacity by time, desired capacity is the maintained count, and the launch template defines each instance.
